alignments.note: Construct noun keeps only its own word. Both written *the*s answer to article morphemes standing in the phrase, so rule 29 supplies none here.
Ordinal adjective attributive to the construct noun, which the ASV renders prenominally.
Article on the rectum takes the *the* standing before its own word; the rectum is rendered arthrously, so nothing is fronted (rule 29).

The attributive's article takes the phrase's remaining written *the*. Rule 47 gives it to the present article morpheme rather than to the construct noun as a supplied determiner, expressly where the head noun is a construct that could take no article of its own, and the *the* stands before *third*, the attributive's own word (rule 29's count). The competing reading, which the accepted alignment took, makes this a supplied *the* on `שַׂר` and marks this article `unrepresented`; it is set aside because a present article morpheme takes its English before a supplied one does.
Agreement article on the attributive: the noun's own article takes the single *the* written for that phrase (rule 47).
Verbless clause with a nominal predicate: the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate name (rule 20), the fronted nominal being the subject.
Construct noun with the supplied *the*, no article morpheme standing in this chain (rule 29).
Noun in apposition; the margin's *chief minister* is read and set aside, the printed text governing (rule 38).
Prepositional predicate takes the construction-supplied copula, headed on the preposition (rule 49); discontinuous under rule 25.
Waw takes the *and* standing between these two numerals (rule 42).

review_notes: Corrected: the opening *The* is moved from a supplied determiner on the construct `שַׂר` to the present article on the attributive `הַשְּׁלִישִׁי`. Rule 47 holds even where the head noun is a construct that could take no article of its own, and a present article morpheme takes the English *the* before a supplied one does; the phrase's two *the*s then answer to its two article morphemes, each standing before its own word.
This is the same count v.8 runs for `הַחֲמִישִׁי ... הַשַּׂר`, where the single *the* stands before *fifth* and the first article takes it.
The ASV marginal note (*Or, chief minister*) was read and set aside; the printed text is aligned (rule 38).
